records.text: White now has a new passed pawn. That matters, but promotion is not promised. Check what could block or capture it.
Black now has a new passed pawn. That matters, but promotion is not promised. Check what could block or capture it.
The better move would have created a passed pawn for White. Study that option with the possible blockers in mind.
The better move would have created a passed pawn for Black. Study that option with the possible blockers in mind.
White has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawn occupies either adjacent file. Make piece support part of the assessment.
Black has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawn occupies either adjacent file. Make piece support part of the assessment.
The better move would have left White with an isolated pawn. Account for that structure without dismissing the whole move.
The better move would have left Black with an isolated pawn. Account for that structure without dismissing the whole move.
White now has doubled pawns. They share a file; assess the position before calling that arrangement a weakness.
Black now has doubled pawns. They share a file; assess the position before calling that arrangement a weakness.
The better move would have doubled White's pawns. Judge the full result, not the pawn shape alone.
The better move would have doubled Black's pawns. Judge the full result, not the pawn shape alone.
White's rook has an open file now. There are no pawns on it. Check what the pieces permit before planning an invasion.
Black's rook has an open file now. There are no pawns on it. Check what the pieces permit before planning an invasion.
The better move would have placed White's rook on an open file. Compare that placement carefully; pawnless does not mean unobstructed.
The better move would have placed Black's rook on an open file. Compare that placement carefully; pawnless does not mean unobstructed.
White's rook occupies a half-open file. None of its own pawns are there, but enemy pawns are. Examine the placement on that basis.
Black's rook occupies a half-open file. None of its own pawns are there, but enemy pawns are. Examine the placement on that basis.
The better move would have put White's rook on a half-open file. Friendly pawns absent, enemy pawns present. Include that in the comparison.
The better move would have put Black's rook on a half-open file. Friendly pawns absent, enemy pawns present. Include that in the comparison.
White's knight is defended now. It had no cover before this move. Learn to notice that change in support.
Black's knight is defended now. It had no cover before this move. Learn to notice that change in support.
White's bishop has gained protection it lacked. Identify the defender and keep track of that connection.
Black's bishop has gained protection it lacked. Identify the defender and keep track of that connection.
White's rook has acquired a defender. That is a concrete change; verify how the new protection works.
Black's rook has acquired a defender. That is a concrete change; verify how the new protection works.
White's queen is no longer undefended. Find its new guard and include that support in future calculations.
Black's queen is no longer undefended. Find its new guard and include that support in future calculations.
The better move would have defended White's unguarded knight. Compare that protection with the position actually reached.
The better move would have defended Black's unguarded knight. Compare that protection with the position actually reached.
The better move would have supplied the missing defender for White's bishop. Notice support as well as attacking chances.
The better move would have supplied the missing defender for Black's bishop. Notice support as well as attacking chances.
White's unprotected rook would have gained a defender with the better move. Put that connection into the analysis.
Black's unprotected rook would have gained a defender with the better move. Put that connection into the analysis.
The better move would have guarded White's undefended queen. That change deserves attention in the comparison.
The better move would have guarded Black's undefended queen. That change deserves attention in the comparison.
White's knight has lost all its defenders. Check whether the opponent can exploit it. Do not confuse unguarded with lost.
Black's knight has lost all its defenders. Check whether the opponent can exploit it. Do not confuse unguarded with lost.
White's bishop has lost its remaining protection. Make a threat check before drawing a conclusion about material.
Black's bishop has lost its remaining protection. Make a threat check before drawing a conclusion about material.
White's rook is undefended after this move. Identify what stopped guarding it, then assess the possible attacks.
Black's rook is undefended after this move. Identify what stopped guarding it, then assess the possible attacks.
White's queen no longer has a defender. That is a fact to account for, not permission to assume it can be won.
Black's queen no longer has a defender. That is a fact to account for, not permission to assume it can be won.
The better move would have removed the last defender of White's knight. Evaluate whether that would be exploitable.
The better move would have removed the last defender of Black's knight. Evaluate whether that would be exploitable.
White's bishop would have become undefended with the better move. Check the actual threats rather than rejecting it on appearance.
Black's bishop would have become undefended with the better move. Check the actual threats rather than rejecting it on appearance.
The better move would have left White's rook without a guard. Assess the consequences; missing protection does not prove a loss.
The better move would have left Black's rook without a guard. Assess the consequences; missing protection does not prove a loss.
The better move would have left White's queen undefended. Include that fact, then verify what the opponent could do.
The better move would have left Black's queen undefended. Include that fact, then verify what the opponent could do.
The knight has developed from its starting square. That is its first departure; now evaluate the square it chose.
A knight leaves its original post for the first time. Check which squares it can reach now.
First move from home for the knight. Check its role from the new square.
First departure for the knight. Inspect its new square before planning its next move.
The bishop has developed from its original square. Follow its diagonals and assess the new placement.
The bishop makes its first move away from its starting post. Trace each diagonal from the new square.
First departure from home for the bishop. Now judge what its new position offers.
The bishop has left its starting square for the first time. Include that development when assessing the move.
The better choice would have developed a knight from its original square. Study that placement alongside the move played.
The better move included a knight's first departure from its starting post. Compare the resulting placement carefully.
The better move would have brought a knight out from its starting square for the first time. Include that in the assessment.
Knight development was part of the stronger choice. It would have moved the knight from its original square for the first time.
The better choice would have developed a bishop from its original square. Examine its placement in that position.
A bishop's first departure from its starting post was the alternative. Study how that development fits the better move.
The better move would have brought a bishop off its starting square for the first time. Compare the resulting positions.
Bishop development belonged to the stronger option. It would have been the bishop's first move from its original square.
This move gives up value compared with the better choice. Work through the alternatives until the difference is clear.
A stronger choice was available. Work through its replies, then compare what this move leaves behind.
The result rates below the best available move. Go back to the choice and examine the replies.
A better choice was available. This move falls short of it; study the resulting positions side by side.
The opponent has an immediate capture. Check that reply before following any longer plan.
A capture is available to the other side now. Account for the exchange; do not assume it gains material.
The next reply can take something. Assess that capture from the opponent's side of the board.
There is a capture straight away for the opponent. Make checking immediate replies a habit.
You used the opponent's last mistake. That is the standard: recognize the chance and act on it.
Well handled. The opponent made an error, and you turned it into a useful opportunity.
Your move takes advantage of the previous error. Keep practicing that connection between their mistake and your response.
The engine prefers a stronger move here. Find it before moving on.
A stronger option existed in this position. Learn why the engine picks it, and make that check a habit.
A stronger move is available in the engine analysis. Set it beside the move played.
The passed pawn has advanced toward promotion. Reassess its protection before planning the next push.
That passer is nearer the last rank now. The advance is real; promotion still has to be earned.
The strongest answer is a check. Calculate the legal replies before going further.
The best reply puts the king in check. Dealing with that check comes before any other plan.
Correct lesson move. Keep the reason for it in focus.
That matches the lesson's intended move. Build understanding alongside the answer.
Yes, the lesson calls for that move. Remember the position as well as the action.
Correct step. Stay with the puzzle; there is more to solve.
That move is right. Finish the calculation for the remaining puzzle.
Well done so far. Keep working through the puzzle's next move.
That matches the opening move in your study. Keep the position firmly linked to it.
Correct repertoire answer. Know where the move belongs, not just what it is.
Your opening recall matches the study. Carry that attention into the next position.
Best choice. Make understanding it the next task.
That meets the standard for Best. Study why it deserves the grade.
A good move. Compare the stronger option without overlooking what this choice gets right.
Sound, though a better choice exists. Learn the improvement and keep going.
